title: 5 questions before building tidy-board
subtitle: Each question comes with context, options and the effect of each choice.

items.title: How do we detect that a branch has already been merged?

fields.label: Context
fields.text: Squash-merge rewrites the commits, so comparing ids is not enough. tidy-board deletes approved branches, and a false "merged" is costly.

choices.label: Ancestor of the base (`git merge-base`)
choices.effect: safe, but does not recognise squash-merge

choices.label: Compare patch-id with the base
choices.effect: recognises a simple squash; fails if a conflict was resolved

choices.label: Ask GitHub (`gh pr list`)
choices.effect: exact, but needs network and login

items.why: covers the most common case without network and without depending on gh.

items.title: What should each branch card show?

fields.label: Context
fields.text: The card must allow a decision in under 30 seconds, without opening the terminal.

choices.label: Name, last commit and whether it is merged
Name, last commit, author, commits ahead and files
All of that plus a summarised diff

items.why: gives the risk context without becoming a code-review screen.

items.title: Which kinds of things may tidy-board delete?

fields.label: Context
fields.text: Each kind has a different risk. You can allow more than one.

items.why: they are local and reversible; remote ones stay out until there is trust.

items.title: What name do you want for the cleanup command?

fields.label: Context
fields.text: Open question: there are no options, the answer is your own text.

items.title: In what order do the cards appear?

fields.label: Context
fields.text: No recommendation: it depends on how you usually clean up.
